     9	/-!
    10	# The divisor subscheme of a widened affine adaptation
    11	
    12	The intrinsic Cartier ideal of a widened adaptation defines a closed divisor subscheme.
    13	Its inverse image over every adapted affine piece is affine, with coordinate ring exactly
    14	the existing `AffAdaptation.colength`.  These spectra form an affine open cover indexed by
    15	the arbitrary widened cover, without a fixed chart partition or `SwallowedBy` hypothesis.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    26	
    27	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    28	
    29	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    30	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    31	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    32	
    33	namespace AffAdaptation
    34	
    35	/-- The closed divisor subscheme cut out by the intrinsic Cartier ideal. -/
    36	noncomputable abbrev divisorSubscheme (A : AffAdaptation D d) : Scheme :=
    37	  A.cartierIdeal.subscheme
    38	
    39	/-- The closed immersion of the divisor subscheme into the relative curve. -/
    40	noncomputable abbrev divisorSubschemeι (A : AffAdaptation D d) :
    41	    A.divisorSubscheme ⟶ relCurve C R :=
    42	  A.cartierIdeal.subschemeι
    43	
    44	instance isClosedImmersion_divisorSubschemeι (A : AffAdaptation D d) :
    45	    IsClosedImmersion A.divisorSubschemeι := by
    46	  infer_instance
    47	
    48	/-- The kernel of the divisor inclusion is the intrinsic Cartier ideal. -/
    49	theorem ker_divisorSubschemeι (A : AffAdaptation D d) :
    50	    A.divisorSubschemeι.ker = A.cartierIdeal :=
    51	  Scheme.IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι _
    52	
    53	/-- The divisor subscheme as a scheme over the affine test base. -/
    54	noncomputable def divisorSubschemeOver (A : AffAdaptation D d) :
    55	    Over (Spec (.of R)) :=
    56	  Over.mk (A.divisorSubschemeι ≫ (relCurve C R ↘ Spec (.of R)))
    57	
    58	/-- Replacing the Cartier ideal by its adapted principal generator identifies the local
    59	quotient algebra with the existing colength algebra. -/
    60	noncomputable def divisorPieceQuotientEquiv [IsProper C.hom]
    61	    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (i : D.index) :
    62	    (Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i) ⧸
    63	      A.cartierIdeal.ideal ⟨D.pieces i, D.isAffineOpen i⟩) ≃ₐ[R]
    64	      A.colength i :=
    65	  Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq R (A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_span_eqn i)
    66	
    67	/-- Sections of the divisor subscheme over a widened affine piece are its recorded
    68	colength algebra. -/
    69	noncomputable def divisorSubschemePieceIso [IsProper C.hom]

    12	`AffAdaptation.ovlColength`.  Under this identification, restriction from either divisor
    13	piece is exactly the corresponding equalizer arrow `toOvlLeft` or `toOvlRight`.
    14	
    15	These comparisons connect the geometric affine cover of the divisor to the pre-existing
    16	Čech algebra and theta descent datum, without changing their carrier or hypotheses.
    17	-/

    22	universe u
    23	
    24	open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace

    28	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

    30	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    31	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    32	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    33

    36	/-- On an adapted overlap, the intrinsic Cartier ideal is the symmetric overlap ideal
    37	already used by the widened equalizer. -/
    38	theorem cartierIdeal_ideal_overlap_eq_ovlIdeal [IsProper C.hom]
    39	    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (i j : D.index) :
    40	    A.cartierIdeal.ideal
    41	        ⟨D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j,
    42	          Over.isAffineOpen_inf C (D.isAffineOpen i) (D.isAffineOpen j)⟩ =
    43	      A.ovlIdeal i j := by
    44	  let U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens :=
    45	    ⟨D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j,
    46	      Over.isAffineOpen_inf C (D.isAffineOpen i) (D.isAffineOpen j)⟩
    47	  let V : (relCurve C R).affineOpens := ⟨D.pieces i, D.isAffineOpen i⟩
    48	  have hUV : U ≤ V := by
    49	    intro x hx
    50	    exact hx.1
    51	  change A.cartierIdeal.ideal U = A.ovlIdeal i j
    52	  calc
    53	    A.cartierIdeal.ideal U =
    54	      (A.cartierIdeal.ideal V).map
    55	        ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
    56	          (homOfLE (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i)).op).hom :=
    57	        (A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal hUV).symm
    58	    _ = Ideal.span {relResAlgHom C R
    59	          (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i)} := by
    60	      rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_span_eqn i, Ideal.map_span, Set.image_singleton]
    61	      rfl
    62	    _ = A.ovlIdeal i j := (A.ovlIdeal_eq_span_left i j).symm
    63	
    64	/-- Sections of the divisor over a pairwise overlap are the symmetric overlap colength
    65	algebra used in `AffAdaptation.gluedSubalgebra`. -/

    67	    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (i j : D.index) :

    69	      A.divisorSubschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)) ≅
    70	      CommRingCat.of (A.ovlColength i j) :=
    71	  A.cartierIdeal.subschemeObjIso
    72	      ⟨D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j,
    73	        Over.isAffineOpen_inf C (D.isAffineOpen i) (D.isAffineOpen j)⟩ ≪≫
    74	    (Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq R

    96	    A.divisorSubscheme.presheaf.map
    97	        (homOfLE (show A.divisorSubschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) ≤

   106	      (A.cartierIdeal.subschemeι_app_surjective

   112	          (((Opens.map A.divisorSubschemeι.base).map
   113	            (homOfLE
   114	              (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i)).op.unop).op) =

   116	          (homOfLE (show A.divisorSubschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) ≤
   117	            A.divisorSubschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ D.pieces i by

   122	  rw [← A.divisorSubschemeι.naturality
   123	    (homOfLE (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i)).op]

   125	  rw [A.divisorSubschemeι_app_pieceIso i]
   126	  apply ConcreteCategory.hom_ext
   127	  intro s
   128	  exact (A.toOvlLeft_mk i j s).symm

     9	/-!
    10	# Faithfully flat descent of modules
    11	
    12	Let `A → B` be a map of commutative rings and let `M` be a `B`-module.  This file defines
    13	descent data on `M` relative to `A → B`, constructs the descended `A`-module `M₀` as an
    14	equalizer submodule of `M`, and proves the two fundamental theorems of flat descent for
    15	modules:
    16	
    17	* **effectivity**: if `B` is flat over `A`, the canonical comparison map
    18	  `B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` is an isomorphism;
    19	* **uniqueness**: if `B` is faithfully flat over `A`, then any `A`-module `N` equipped with
    20	  a `B`-module isomorphism `B ⊗[A] N ≃ M` matching the descent datum is canonically
    21	  isomorphic to `M₀`.  The engine is the degree `≤ 1` exactness of the Amitsur complex
    22	  `0 → N → B ⊗[A] N ⇉ B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] N`.
    23	
    24	## Design notes
    25	
    26	* **Comodule form of a descent datum.**  Classically a descent datum on `M` is a
    27	  `B ⊗[A] B`-module isomorphism `φ : M ⊗[A] B ≃ B ⊗[A] M` satisfying a cocycle condition
    28	  over the triple tensor product.  We use the equivalent *comodule* (Sweedler-coring)
    29	  presentation: a `B`-linear coaction `δ : M →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] M` (with `B` acting on the left
    30	  tensor factor of the target) such that
    31	  - (`counit`) the action map `B ⊗[A] M → M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`, retracts `δ`, and
    32	  - (`coassoc`) the two natural liftings of `δ` to `B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] M` agree on the image
    33	    of `δ`.
    34	
    35	  The dictionary: given `φ`, set `δ m := φ (m ⊗ₜ 1)`; then `B ⊗ B`-linearity of `φ` makes
    36	  `δ` `B`-linear and recovers `φ` via `φ (m ⊗ₜ b) = (1 ⊗ b) • δ m`, the cocycle condition
    37	  becomes `coassoc`, and the standard normalization becomes `counit`.  Conversely the `φ`
    38	  associated to a coaction is automatically invertible.  This presentation avoids putting
    39	  (several!) `B ⊗[A] B`-module structures on `B ⊗[A] M` and `M ⊗[A] B`, which do not exist
    40	  as mathlib instances.  For a unit `u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` whose associated `φ` is
    41	  `u • ·` on `M = B`, the coaction is `δ x = u.val * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`.
    42	
    43	* **The descended module** is the equalizer `M₀ = {m : M | δ m = 1 ⊗ₜ m}`, an `A`-submodule
    44	  of `M`, realized as the kernel of the `A`-linear map `δ - (1 ⊗ₜ ·)`.
    45	
    46	* **Effectivity requires only flatness.**  The comparison `B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` is an isomorphism
    47	  whenever `B` is flat over `A`: the counit and coassociativity laws make the augmented
    48	  complex `M₀ → M ⇉ B ⊗[A] M` contractible after applying `B ⊗[A] -` (the contraction being
    49	  the action maps), and flatness identifies `B ⊗[A] M₀` with the corresponding kernel.
    50	  Faithful flatness enters only for uniqueness (the Amitsur exactness `N ≅ (B ⊗[A] N)₀`).
    51	
    52	* Everything is pinned to a single universe `u`; multi-universe binders interact badly with
    53	  the tensor-product instance search in downstream files.
    54	
    55	## Main declarations
    56	
    57	* `Module.actionMap A B M : B ⊗[A] M →ₗ[B] M`: the action map `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`.
    58	* `Module.DescentDatum A B M`: descent data on the `B`-module `M` relative to `A → B`,
    59	  in comodule form.
    60	* `Module.DescentDatum.baseChange A B N`: the canonical descent datum on `B ⊗[A] N`.
    61	* `Module.DescentDatum.descended`: the descended `A`-submodule `M₀`.
    62	* `Module.DescentDatum.comparison`: the canonical map `B ⊗[A] M₀ →ₗ[B] M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`.
    63	* `Module.DescentDatum.comparison_bijective`: **effectivity** — `comparison` is bijective
    64	  when `B` is a flat `A`-module.
    65	* `Module.DescentDatum.descentEquiv : B ⊗[A] M₀ ≃ₗ[B] M`: the comparison isomorphism.
    66	* `Module.DescentDatum.exact_mk_coactionSub`: degree `≤ 1` **Amitsur exactness** for a
    67	  faithfully flat `A → B`.
    68	* `Module.DescentDatum.unitEquiv : N ≃ₗ[A] (baseChange A B N).descended`: the unit of
    69	  descent is an isomorphism (faithfully flat case).
    70	* `Module.DescentDatum.equivDescended`: **uniqueness** — an `A`-module `N` with a
    71	  datum-compatible isomorphism `B ⊗[A] N ≃ₗ[B] M` is canonically `A`-isomorphic to `M₀`.
    72	  Two descents of the same datum are therefore canonically isomorphic.
    73	-/

    84	/-- The `B`-linear action map `B ⊗[A] M →ₗ[B] M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`, of a `B`-module `M`. -/
    85	noncomputable def actionMap : B ⊗[A] M →ₗ[B] M :=
    86	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B (LinearMap.id (R := A) (M := M))
    87	
    88	@[simp] theorem actionMap_tmul (b : B) (m : M) : actionMap A B M (b ⊗ₜ m) = b • m := rfl
    89	
    90	theorem actionMap_one_tmul (m : M) : actionMap A B M (1 ⊗ₜ m) = m := by simp
    91	
    92	variable {A B M}

    94	section actionMap
    95	
    96	variable {X Y : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module A X]
    97	
    98	/-- Naturality of the action map in `B`-linear maps. -/
    99	theorem actionMap_baseChange [Module B X] [IsScalarTower A B X]
   100	    [AddCommGroup Y] [Module A Y] [Module B Y] [IsScalarTower A B Y]
   101	    (g : X →ₗ[B] Y) (x : B ⊗[A] X) :
   102	    actionMap A B Y ((g.restrictScalars A).baseChange B x) = g (actionMap A B X x) := by
   103	  induction x with
   104	  | zero => simp
   105	  | tmul b m => simp
   106	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
   107	
   108	/-- The action map of `B ⊗[A] X` retracts the base change of `x ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ x`. -/
   109	theorem actionMap_baseChange_mk (x : B ⊗[A] X) :
   110	    actionMap A B (B ⊗[A] X) ((TensorProduct.mk A B X 1).baseChange B x) = x := by
   111	  induction x with
   112	  | zero => simp
   113	  | tmul b m => simp [TensorProduct.smul_tmul']
   114	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
   115	
   116	end actionMap
   117	
   118	variable (A B M) in
   119	/-- A descent datum on a `B`-module `M` relative to `A → B`, in comodule (Sweedler-coring)
   120	form: a `B`-linear coaction `δ : M → B ⊗[A] M` (`B` acting through the left tensor factor
   121	of the target) that is counital and coassociative.  This is equivalent to the classical
   122	formulation via a `B ⊗[A] B`-linear cocycle isomorphism `M ⊗[A] B ≃ B ⊗[A] M`; see the
   123	module docstring for the dictionary. -/
   124	structure DescentDatum where
   125	  /-- The coaction of the descent datum. -/
   126	  coaction : M →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] M
   127	  /-- The action map retracts the coaction. -/
   128	  counit (m : M) : actionMap A B M (coaction m) = m
   129	  /-- Coassociativity: the two liftings of the coaction to `B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] M` agree on
   130	  coaction values.  In the classical dictionary this is the cocycle condition. -/
   131	  coassoc (m : M) :
   132	    (coaction.restrictScalars A).baseChange B (coaction m) =
   133	      (TensorProduct.mk A B M 1).baseChange B (coaction m)
   134	
   135	namespace DescentDatum
   136	
   137	variable (A B) in
   138	/-- The canonical descent datum on a base change `B ⊗[A] N`, with coaction
   139	`b ⊗ₜ n ↦ b ⊗ₜ 1 ⊗ₜ n`. -/
   140	@[simps coaction]
   141	noncomputable def baseChange (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] :
   142	    DescentDatum A B (B ⊗[A] N) where
   143	  coaction := (TensorProduct.mk A B N 1).baseChange B
   144	  counit x := by
   145	    induction x with
   146	    | zero => simp
   147	    | tmul b n => simp [TensorProduct.smul_tmul']
   148	    | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
   149	  coassoc x := by
   150	    induction x with
   151	    | zero => simp
   152	    | tmul b n => simp
   153	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
   154	
   155	variable (D : DescentDatum A B M)
   156	
   157	/-- The `A`-linear difference between the coaction and the canonical map `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`;
   158	its kernel is the descended module. -/
   159	def coactionSub : M →ₗ[A] B ⊗[A] M :=
   160	  D.coaction.restrictScalars A - TensorProduct.mk A B M 1
   161	
   162	@[simp] theorem coactionSub_apply (m : M) : D.coactionSub m = D.coaction m - 1 ⊗ₜ m := rfl
   163	
   164	/-- The descended `A`-module of a descent datum: the equalizer
   165	`M₀ = {m : M | δ m = 1 ⊗ₜ m}`. -/
   166	def descended : Submodule A M := LinearMap.ker D.coactionSub
   167	
   168	theorem mem_descended {m : M} : m ∈ D.descended ↔ D.coaction m = 1 ⊗ₜ m := by
   169	  rw [descended, LinearMap.mem_ker, coactionSub_apply, sub_eq_zero]
   170	
   171	/-- The canonical comparison map `B ⊗[A] M₀ →ₗ[B] M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`.  Flat descent
   172	(`comparison_bijective`) asserts this is an isomorphism when `B` is flat over `A`. -/
   173	noncomputable def comparison : B ⊗[A] D.descended →ₗ[B] M :=
   174	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B D.descended.subtype
   175	
   176	@[simp] theorem comparison_tmul (b : B) (m : D.descended) :
   177	    D.comparison (b ⊗ₜ m) = b • (m : M) := rfl
   178	
   179	theorem comparison_eq_actionMap (x : B ⊗[A] D.descended) :
   180	    D.comparison x = actionMap A B M (D.descended.subtype.lTensor B x) := by
   181	  induction x with
   182	  | zero => simp
   183	  | tmul b m => simp
   184	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
   185	
   186	private theorem coactionSub_lTensor_apply (x : B ⊗[A] M) :
   187	    D.coactionSub.lTensor B x =
   188	      (D.coaction.restrictScalars A).baseChange B x -
   189	        (TensorProduct.mk A B M 1).baseChange B x := by
   190	  induction x with
   191	  | zero => simp
   192	  | tmul b m => simp [TensorProduct.tmul_sub]

   197	/-- The coaction retracts onto the kernel of `coactionSub ⊗ B`: any `x : B ⊗[A] M` on which
   198	the two liftings agree is a coaction value, namely of `actionMap x`.  This is the
   199	contracting-homotopy computation at the heart of both effectivity and Amitsur exactness. -/
   200	theorem coaction_actionMap {x : B ⊗[A] M}
   201	    (hx : (D.coaction.restrictScalars A).baseChange B x =
   202	      (TensorProduct.mk A B M 1).baseChange B x) :
   203	    D.coaction (actionMap A B M x) = x :=
   204	  (actionMap_baseChange D.coaction x).symm.trans <| by rw [hx, actionMap_baseChange_mk]

   206	/-- **Effectivity of flat descent for modules**: for `B` flat over `A`, the canonical map
   207	`B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` out of the descended module is bijective. -/
   208	theorem comparison_bijective [Module.Flat A B] : Function.Bijective D.comparison := by
   209	  have hexact : Function.Exact (D.descended.subtype.lTensor B) (D.coactionSub.lTensor B) :=
   210	    Module.Flat.lTensor_exact B D.coactionSub.exact_subtype_ker_map
   211	  have hinj : Function.Injective (D.descended.subtype.lTensor B) :=
   212	    Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _ D.descended.injective_subtype
   213	  have key : ∀ y : B ⊗[A] D.descended,
   214	      D.coaction (D.comparison y) = D.descended.subtype.lTensor B y := by
   215	    intro y
   216	    rw [comparison_eq_actionMap]
   217	    refine D.coaction_actionMap (sub_eq_zero.mp ?_)
   218	    rw [← coactionSub_lTensor_apply]
   219	    exact hexact.apply_apply_eq_zero y
   220	  constructor
   221	  · intro y z hyz
   222	    exact hinj (by rw [← key, ← key, hyz])
   223	  · intro m
   224	    have hm : D.coactionSub.lTensor B (D.coaction m) = 0 := by
   225	      rw [coactionSub_lTensor_apply, D.coassoc m, sub_self]
   226	    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (hexact _).mp hm
   227	    refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
   228	    have hcoact : D.coaction (D.comparison y) = D.coaction m := by rw [key y, hy]
   229	    have := congrArg (actionMap A B M) hcoact
   230	    rwa [D.counit, D.counit] at this

   233	noncomputable def descentEquiv [Module.Flat A B] : B ⊗[A] D.descended ≃ₗ[B] M :=
   234	  LinearEquiv.ofBijective D.comparison D.comparison_bijective

   243	/-- **Amitsur exactness in degrees `≤ 1`**: for a faithfully flat `A → B` and any
   244	`A`-module `N`, the sequence `0 → N → B ⊗[A] N ⇉ B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] N` is exact; here the pair
   245	of arrows is encoded by the single map `coactionSub` of the canonical descent datum, whose
   246	kernel is the equalizer. -/
   247	theorem exact_mk_coactionSub (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] :
   248	    Function.Exact (TensorProduct.mk A B N 1) (baseChange A B N).coactionSub := by
   249	  apply (Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_exact_iff_exact A B _ _).mp
   250	  intro z
   251	  constructor
   252	  · intro hz
   253	    refine ⟨actionMap A B (B ⊗[A] N) z, ?_⟩
   254	    have hx := (baseChange A B N).coaction_actionMap (x := z) (sub_eq_zero.mp (by
   255	      rw [← coactionSub_lTensor_apply]; exact hz))
   256	    rw [baseChange_coaction] at hx
   257	    rw [← LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
   258	    exact hx
   259	  · rintro ⟨x, rfl⟩
   260	    rw [coactionSub_lTensor_apply, sub_eq_zero]
   261	    induction x with
   262	    | zero => simp
   263	    | tmul b n => simp
   264	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
   265	
   266	/-- The unit of descent: for a faithfully flat `A → B`, the canonical map identifies an
   267	`A`-module `N` with the descended module of the canonical descent datum on `B ⊗[A] N`.
   268	This is the degree `0` consequence of Amitsur exactness. -/
   269	noncomputable def unitEquiv (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] :
   270	    N ≃ₗ[A] (baseChange A B N).descended := by
   271	  refine LinearEquiv.ofBijective
   272	    ((TensorProduct.mk A B N 1).codRestrict (baseChange A B N).descended fun n => ?_)
   273	    ⟨fun n n' h => ?_, fun y => ?_⟩
   274	  · rw [mem_descended]
   275	    simp
   276	  · exact Module.FaithfullyFlat.tensorProduct_mk_injective (A := A) (B := B) N
   277	      (congrArg Subtype.val h)
   278	  · have h0 : (baseChange A B N).coactionSub (y : B ⊗[A] N) = 0 := LinearMap.mem_ker.mp y.2
   279	    obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := (exact_mk_coactionSub N (y : B ⊗[A] N)).mp h0
   280	    exact ⟨n, Subtype.ext hn⟩
   281	
   282	@[simp] theorem unitEquiv_apply_coe (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] (n : N) :
   283	    (unitEquiv (A := A) (B := B) N n : B ⊗[A] N) = 1 ⊗ₜ n := rfl
   284	
   285	variable {N : Type u} [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
   286	
   287	/-- **Uniqueness of descent**: if `N` is an `A`-module and `e : B ⊗[A] N ≃ₗ[B] M`
   288	intertwines the canonical descent datum on `B ⊗[A] N` with `D`, then `N` is canonically
   289	`A`-isomorphic to the descended module of `D`.  In particular two descents of the same
   290	datum are canonically isomorphic (compose one such equivalence with the inverse of the
   291	other). -/
   292	noncomputable def equivDescended (e : (B ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[B] M)
   293	    (he : ∀ x : B ⊗[A] N,
   294	      D.coaction (e x) = ((e : B ⊗[A] N →ₗ[B] M).restrictScalars A).baseChange B
   295	        ((baseChange A B N).coaction x)) :
   296	    N ≃ₗ[A] D.descended := by
   297	  refine (unitEquiv N).trans <|
   298	    ((e.restrictScalars A).submoduleMap (baseChange A B N).descended).trans
   299	      (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ ?_)
   300	  have hinj : Function.Injective
   301	      (((e : B ⊗[A] N →ₗ[B] M).restrictScalars A).baseChange B) := by
   302	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
   303	    exact Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _ e.injective
   304	  ext m
   305	  simp only [Submodule.mem_map]
   306	  constructor
   307	  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
   308	    rw [mem_descended] at hx ⊢
   309	    change D.coaction (e x) = 1 ⊗ₜ (e x)
   310	    rw [he x, hx]
   311	    simp
   312	  · intro hm
   313	    refine ⟨e.symm m, ?_, e.apply_symm_apply m⟩
   314	    rw [mem_descended] at hm ⊢
   315	    apply hinj
   316	    have := he (e.symm m)
   317	    rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply] at this
   318	    rw [← this, hm]
   319	    simp
   320	
   321	@[simp] theorem equivDescended_apply_coe (e : (B ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[B] M)
   322	    (he : ∀ x : B ⊗[A] N,
   323	      D.coaction (e x) = ((e : B ⊗[A] N →ₗ[B] M).restrictScalars A).baseChange B
   324	        ((baseChange A B N).coaction x)) (n : N) :
   325	    (D.equivDescended e he n : M) = e (1 ⊗ₜ n) := rfl

     8	/-!
     9	# The intrinsic theta Cech equalizer over the widened colength algebra
    10	
    11	The intrinsic piece and overlap quotients of `DivisorFamilyAffThetaDescent` are modules over
    12	different local colength algebras. This file restricts all of those actions to the single
    13	widened equalizer algebra `A_D = gluedSubalgebra A`. The two overlap restrictions then become
    14	`A_D`-linear maps, and the intrinsic theta module is their kernel in `A_D`-modules.
    15	
    16	The final declarations give the resulting equalizer its universal property. This is the
    17	module-descent input needed to compare the intrinsic theta line with its piecewise base
    18	changes and descend invertibility, without a `ChartTyping` or any additional hypothesis.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace
    26	
    27	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    28	
    29	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    30	
    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    32	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    33	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] [IsProper C.hom]
    34	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    35	
    36	namespace AffAdaptation

    38	attribute [local instance] thetaPieceQuotientModule thetaOverlapQuotientModule
    39	
    40	/-- Restriction of the widened equalizer algebra to one overlap colength algebra. -/
    41	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap (A : AffAdaptation D d) (i j : D.index) :
    42	    ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
    43	  (A.toOvlLeft i j).comp (A.gluedSubalgebraPieceMap i)
    44	
    45	omit [IsProper C.hom] in
    46	/-- The overlap algebra map is independent of whether it is evaluated through the left or
    47	right piece. This is exactly the defining equalizer relation of `A_D`. -/
    48	lemma gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap_eq_right (A : AffAdaptation D d) (i j : D.index) :
    49	    A.gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap i j =
    50	      (A.toOvlRight i j).comp (A.gluedSubalgebraPieceMap j) := by
    51	  ext c
    52	  change A.toOvlLeft i j (c.1 i) = A.toOvlRight i j (c.1 j)
    53	  exact (A.mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (c : A.chartProd)).mp c.2 (i, j)
    54	
    55	/-- An overlap theta quotient, restricted to an `A_D`-module through the common overlap
    56	algebra map. -/
    57	@[reducible]
    58	noncomputable def thetaOverlapQuotientGluedModule (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    59	    (i j : D.index) :
    60	    Module ↥(gluedSubalgebra A)
    61	      (A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j) :=
    62	  letI : Module (A.ovlColength i j) (A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j) :=
    63	    A.thetaOverlapQuotientModule (π := π) a i j
    64	  Module.compHom (A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j)
    65	    (A.gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap i j).toRingHom
    66	
    67	attribute [local instance] thetaPieceQuotientGluedModule
    68	  thetaOverlapQuotientGluedModule
    69	
    70	/-- The intrinsic theta equalizer carries its canonical module structure over the widened
    71	colength algebra outside this construction file as well. -/
    72	@[reducible]
    73	noncomputable instance intrinsicThetaGluedOverModule (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) :
    74	    Module ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) (A.IntrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a) :=
    75	  letI : ∀ j, Module ↥(gluedSubalgebra A)
    76	      (A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j) :=
    77	    fun j => A.thetaPieceQuotientGluedModule (π := π) a j
    78	  Submodule.module (A.intrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a)
    79	
    80	/-- The left piece-to-overlap restriction as an `A_D`-linear map. -/
    81	noncomputable def thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    82	    (i j : D.index) :
    83	    A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a i →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
    84	      A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j where
    85	  toFun := A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j
    86	  map_add' := (A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j).map_add
    87	  map_smul' := by
    88	    intro c x
    89	    change A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j (c.1 i • x) =
    90	      A.gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap i j c •
    91	        A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j x
    92	    rw [A.thetaToOverlapLeft_smul]
    93	    rfl
    94	
    95	/-- The right piece-to-overlap restriction as an `A_D`-linear map. -/
    96	noncomputable def thetaToOverlapRightGlued (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    97	    (i j : D.index) :
    98	    A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
    99	      A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j where
   100	  toFun := A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j
   101	  map_add' := (A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j).map_add
   102	  map_smul' := by
   103	    intro c x
   104	    change A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j (c.1 j • x) =
   105	      A.gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap i j c •
   106	        A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j x
   107	    rw [A.thetaToOverlapRight_smul]
   108	    rw [A.gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap_eq_right i j]
   109	    rfl

   111	/-- The left arrow of the intrinsic theta descent fork in `A_D`-modules. -/
   112	noncomputable def thetaIntrinsicDeltaLeftGlued (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) :
   113	    A.ThetaPieceProd (π := π) a →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   114	      A.ThetaOverlapProd (π := π) a :=
   115	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>
   116	    A.thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (π := π) a p.1 p.2 ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
   117	
   118	/-- The right arrow of the intrinsic theta descent fork in `A_D`-modules. -/
   119	noncomputable def thetaIntrinsicDeltaRightGlued (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) :
   120	    A.ThetaPieceProd (π := π) a →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   121	      A.ThetaOverlapProd (π := π) a :=
   122	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>
   123	    A.thetaToOverlapRightGlued (π := π) a p.1 p.2 ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   124	
   125	/-- The kernel of the intrinsic theta descent fork, formed in `A_D`-modules. -/
   126	noncomputable def intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) :
   127	    Submodule ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) (A.ThetaPieceProd (π := π) a) :=
   128	  LinearMap.ker (A.thetaIntrinsicDeltaLeftGlued (π := π) a -
   129	    A.thetaIntrinsicDeltaRightGlued (π := π) a)
   130	
   131	/-- Membership in the `A_D`-linear kernel is pairwise equality on overlaps. -/
   132	lemma mem_intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver_iff (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
   133	    (s : A.ThetaPieceProd (π := π) a) :
   134	    s ∈ A.intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver (π := π) a ↔
   135	      ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   136	        A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a p.1 p.2 (s p.1) =
   137	          A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   138	  simp only [intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply,
   139	    sub_eq_zero, funext_iff, thetaIntrinsicDeltaLeftGlued,
   140	    thetaIntrinsicDeltaRightGlued, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   141	    Function.comp_apply, thetaToOverlapLeftGlued,
   142	    thetaToOverlapRightGlued]
   143	  rfl
   144	
   145	/-- The previously constructed intrinsic theta `A_D`-module is exactly the kernel of the
   146	`A_D`-linear descent fork. -/
   147	theorem intrinsicThetaGluedOver_eq_ker (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) :
   148	    A.intrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a =
   149	      A.intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver (π := π) a := by
   150	  ext s
   151	  change s ∈ A.intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule (π := π) a ↔ _
   152	  rw [A.mem_intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule_iff,
   153	    A.mem_intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver_iff]

   155	/-- Projection of the intrinsic theta equalizer to one piece quotient. -/
   156	noncomputable def intrinsicThetaGluedToPiece (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
   157	    (j : D.index) :
   158	    A.IntrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   159	      A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j :=
   160	  LinearMap.proj j ∘ₗ (A.intrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a).subtype
   161	
   162	/-- The piece projections from the intrinsic theta equalizer agree on every overlap. -/
   163	theorem intrinsicThetaGluedToPiece_overlap (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
   164	    (i j : D.index) :
   165	    A.thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ
   166	        A.intrinsicThetaGluedToPiece (π := π) a i =
   167	      A.thetaToOverlapRightGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ
   168	        A.intrinsicThetaGluedToPiece (π := π) a j := by
   169	  apply LinearMap.ext
   170	  intro x
   171	  exact (A.mem_intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule_iff (π := π) a _).mp x.2 (i, j)

   175	variable (A : AffAdaptation D d)
   176	variable {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M]
   177	  [Module ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) M]

   179	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 200000 in
   180	-- The nested dependent-product module action exceeds the default instance-search budget.
   181	/-- A compatible family of `A_D`-linear maps to the piece theta quotients factors through
   182	the intrinsic theta equalizer. -/
   183	noncomputable def intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift (a : ℕ)
   184	    (f : ∀ j : D.index, M →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   185	      A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j)
   186	    (hf : ∀ i j : D.index,
   187	      A.thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f i =
   188	        A.thetaToOverlapRightGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f j) :
   189	    M →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   190	      A.IntrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a where
   191	  toFun x := ⟨fun j => f j x, by
   192	    apply (A.mem_intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule_iff (π := π) a _).mpr
   193	    rintro ⟨i, j⟩
   194	    exact LinearMap.congr_fun (hf i j) x⟩
   195	  map_add' x y := by
   196	    apply Subtype.ext
   197	    funext j
   198	    exact (f j).map_add x y
   199	  map_smul' c x := by
   200	    apply Subtype.ext
   201	    funext j
   202	    exact (f j).map_smul c x
   203	
   204	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 200000 in
   205	-- The statement unfolds the same nested dependent-product module action as the lift.
   206	@[simp]
   207	lemma intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift_apply (a : ℕ)
   208	    (f : ∀ j : D.index, M →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   209	      A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j)
   210	    (hf : ∀ i j : D.index,
   211	      A.thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f i =
   212	        A.thetaToOverlapRightGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f j)
   213	    (x : M) (j : D.index) :
   214	    (A.intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift (π := π) a f hf x :
   215	      A.ThetaPieceProd (π := π) a) j = f j x := by
   216	  rfl

   218	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 200000 in
   219	-- Comparing the two dependent-product linear maps needs the lift's instance-search budget.
   220	/-- The compatible-family lift is the unique `A_D`-linear map with the prescribed piece
   221	projections. -/
   222	theorem intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift_unique (a : ℕ)
   223	    (f : ∀ j : D.index, M →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   224	      A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j)
   225	    (hf : ∀ i j : D.index,
   226	      A.thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f i =
   227	        A.thetaToOverlapRightGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f j)
   228	    (g : M →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   229	      A.IntrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a)
   230	    (hg : ∀ j : D.index,
   231	      A.intrinsicThetaGluedToPiece (π := π) a j ∘ₗ g = f j) :
   232	    g = A.intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift (π := π) a f hf := by
   233	  apply LinearMap.ext
   234	  intro x
   235	  apply Subtype.ext
   236	  funext j
   237	  exact LinearMap.congr_fun (hg j) x

    12	# Intrinsic theta descent on a widened divisor cover
    13	
    14	For an arbitrary affine piece `U_j`, the restriction of `O(a Theta)` to the divisor is
    15	the genuine module
    16	
    17	`Gamma(U_j, O(a Theta)) / (f_j) Gamma(U_j, O(a Theta))`.
    18	
    19	Unlike the older chart-typed theta module, this quotient does not choose a trivialization
    20	of the line bundle on `U_j`.  Restriction to `U_i inter U_j` sends the equation-generated
    21	submodule into the symmetric overlap ideal, so the piece quotients have two canonical
    22	overlap maps.  Their equalizer is the intrinsic theta restriction on the widened divisor.
    23	
    24	The construction below supplies the module that the widened equalizer algebra acts on.
    25	It is the chart-free input for proving invertibility and identifying the result with the
    26	cover-independent high-window quotient.

   230	theorem thetaSectionsToOverlapLeft_vanishing_le (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)

   232	    A.thetaPieceVanishing (π := π) a i ≤

   236	      (⊤ : Submodule Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i) (A.ThetaPieceSections (π := π) a i)) ≤
   237	    Submodule.comap (A.thetaSectionsToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j)

   239	        (⊤ : Submodule Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)
   240	          (A.ThetaOverlapSections (π := π) a i j)))
   241	  rw [Submodule.smul_le]
   242	  intro r hr s _
   243	  change A.thetaSectionsToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j (r • s) ∈
   244	    A.ovlIdeal i j •
   245	      (⊤ : Submodule Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)
   246	        (A.ThetaOverlapSections (π := π) a i j))

   249	  rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at hr

    11	/-!
    12	# Intrinsic theta restrictions on widened divisor-family pieces
    13	
    14	The widened cover of `AffAdaptation` consists of arbitrary affine opens.  It therefore
    15	cannot use a pinned-chart trivialization of the theta cocycle.  Instead, on each piece
    16	`D.pieces j` we choose the affine sections model of the intrinsic cocycle-glued theta
    17	line bundle `(thetaChartDatum C R π a).sheaf`.  Its sections are an invertible module
    18	over the piece ring.
    19	
    20	Base change along the quotient
    21	`Gamma(D.pieces j) -> A.colength j = Gamma(D.pieces j) / (A.eqn j)` gives the intrinsic
    22	restriction of the theta line bundle to the piece of the finite divisor.  Invertibility
    23	is preserved by this base change.  A widened certificate then makes the colength algebra
    24	finite projective over `R`, so the existing invertible-module transfer gives finite and
    25	projective `R`-modules without any chart typing or additional hypothesis.
